minutes.headline: Sewer Commission seated a new member, elected officers, and sent a new reserve capacity fee to legal review.
minutes.summary: New member Troy Daniels was welcomed and the commission elected a chair, vice chair and clerk. It reviewed inflow and infiltration inspections in the Whalom area, the engineering RFP for the Lakeview and Pratt extensions, a proposed reserve capacity fee, and grease trap permit fee tiers. Prior minutes were approved and invoices were reviewed.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission sent proposed reserve capacity fee language to legal review, aiming to have the fee in place by the end of June.
The commission elected a chair, a vice chair (one member opposed) and a clerk (unanimous) after welcoming a new member.
Members leaned toward advertising the Lakeview and Pratt extension engineering RFP openly rather than limiting it to two firms.
A meeting was set for Wednesday June 4 at the DPW to decide how to release the engineering RFP.
Grease trap reminder letters and a DVD will go out first, followed by visits to establishments; Small Water is invited to the June 10 meeting.

why_it_matters: A reserve capacity fee on new connections would help cover the town's annual capacity cost to Fitchburg, so it bears on what sewer users and new builders pay.
Grease trap permit fees depend on reporting compliance, so food establishments face tiered costs and inspection visits.
watch_next: Wednesday June 4 at 5:00 at the DPW: meeting on how to release the engineering RFP.
June 10 meeting: Small Water is invited, with a proposal beforehand; legal review of the fee language is due by end of June.
